unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Transportation economics is concerned mainly with:
options: Efficient allocation of scarce resources among transport alternatives
explanation: It supports investment and policy decisions.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Transport is described as a derived demand because:
options: It is desired for its own sake
It arises from the need to reach activities at other locations
explanation: Travel is rarely wanted for itself.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Opportunity cost of a transport investment is:
options: The value of the best alternative use of the same resources
explanation: It underlies all economic evaluation.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Economic analysis differs from financial analysis because it:
options: Considers costs and benefits to society including externalities
Considers only cash flows to the operator
explanation: Shadow prices may replace market prices.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Consumer surplus in transport is:
options: The difference between what users are willing to pay and what they actually pay
explanation: Improvements increase it through lower generalised cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Generalised cost of travel combines:
options: Money cost and the value of travel time and other disutilities
explanation: It is the basis of demand modelling.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: A public good characteristic seen in some transport facilities is:
options: Non excludability, making user charging difficult
explanation: This justifies public provision or subsidy.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Natural monopoly conditions in transport arise when:
options: Large fixed costs and declining average cost make one supplier cheapest
explanation: Railways and pipelines exhibit this tendency.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: Discounting future costs and benefits is done because:
options: Money available now is worth more than the same amount later
explanation: The discount rate reflects the opportunity cost of capital.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: The present worth of a future amount F after n years at interest rate i is:
explanation: This is the single payment present worth factor.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: Net present value of a project is:
options: The discounted benefits minus the discounted costs
explanation: A positive NPV indicates an economically worthwhile project.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: The internal rate of return of a project is the discount rate at which:
options: The net present value becomes zero
explanation: It is compared with the minimum attractive rate of return.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: Equivalent uniform annual cost is useful for comparing alternatives with:
explanation: It converts all cash flows to an annual basis.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: The capital recovery factor converts:
options: An annual series into a future sum
A present amount into a uniform annual series
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: Salvage value in economic analysis represents:
options: The value of an asset at the end of the analysis period
explanation: It is discounted back as a benefit.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: A high discount rate in transport appraisal tends to:
options: Disadvantage projects with long term benefits and high initial cost
explanation: Choice of rate is therefore a policy decision.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: Sensitivity analysis in project evaluation examines:
options: How the results change when key assumptions vary
explanation: It identifies critical variables and risks.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: A benefit cost ratio greater than one indicates:
options: The discounted benefits exceed the discounted costs
explanation: Ranking by BCR suits budget constrained selection.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: Typical user benefits of a highway improvement include:
options: Savings in travel time, vehicle operating cost and accidents
explanation: These are quantified over the analysis period.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: Value of travel time savings is usually derived from:
options: Wage rates and stated or revealed preference studies
explanation: Business travel time is valued higher than leisure.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: The rule of half in benefit estimation is applied to:
options: Generated or induced traffic, which gains on average half the cost saving
explanation: Existing users receive the full saving.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: A do nothing or base case is required in appraisal because:
options: Benefits are measured as the difference from the without project situation
explanation: Incremental analysis avoids double counting.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: Multi criteria analysis is used when:
options: Important impacts cannot readily be expressed in money terms
explanation: Weights are assigned to criteria such as equity and environment.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: Double counting in benefit cost analysis occurs if:
options: The same benefit is counted both as user savings and as land value increase
explanation: Land value change largely capitalises user benefits.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: Distributional analysis in transport appraisal examines:
options: Who gains and who loses from the project
explanation: Equity considerations may affect the decision.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: The analysis period for a major transport project is usually taken as:
options: The design or economic life of the asset, commonly 20 to 30 years
explanation: Residual value covers benefits beyond the horizon.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: A project with a high NPV but a lower BCR than another may still be preferred when:
options: Capital is not constrained and total welfare gain matters most
explanation: Under budget constraints BCR ranking is more appropriate.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem: A positive net present value indicates an economically worthwhile project.
explanation: Discounted benefits exceed discounted costs at the chosen discount rate.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Role of economics in transportation decision making
stem: Financial analysis and economic analysis of a transport project always give the same result.
explanation: Economic analysis includes externalities and uses shadow prices, unlike financial analysis.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem:
Assertion (A): The rule of half is applied to induced traffic when estimating benefits.
Reason (R): New trips gain on average only half of the reduction in generalised cost enjoyed by existing users.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: It follows from the linear demand curve assumption.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Time value of money and economic evaluation criteria
stem:
Assertion (A): A high discount rate disadvantages projects whose benefits accrue far in the future.
Reason (R): Discounting reduces the present value of distant benefits much more strongly than near ones.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: The choice of rate is a policy issue.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

unit_title: Introductory Concepts in Transportation Decision Making
topic: Benefit cost analysis and project appraisal
stem: Which are user benefits typically quantified in highway project appraisal?
explanation: Land acquisition is a project cost, not a benefit.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 1

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Fixed costs in transport operations are those that:
options: Do not vary with the level of output in the short run
explanation: Depreciation, insurance and licence fees are examples.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Variable costs of vehicle operation include:
options: Fuel, tyres, lubricants and distance related maintenance
explanation: They rise directly with kilometres run.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Marginal cost is defined as:
options: The additional cost of producing one more unit of output
explanation: Efficient pricing is based on marginal cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: A sunk cost in transport investment appraisal:
options: Has already been incurred and should not affect future decisions
explanation: Only incremental future costs are relevant.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: External costs of transport are those:
options: Imposed on society but not borne by the traveller
explanation: Congestion, pollution and accident externalities are examples.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Joint costs in transport arise when:
options: One operation produces two outputs, such as a haul and a backhaul
explanation: Allocation between the outputs is arbitrary.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Common costs differ from joint costs because they:
options: Are shared by several services but not produced in fixed proportions
explanation: Track costs shared by many trains are an example.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Short run marginal cost differs from long run marginal cost because in the short run:
options: Capacity is fixed and cannot be adjusted
explanation: Congestion charges reflect short run marginal cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Economies of scale in transport exist when:
options: Average cost falls as output increases
explanation: Large fixed infrastructure costs cause this.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Economies of density in a transport network refer to:
options: Falling unit costs as traffic increases on a network of fixed size
explanation: Higher load factors spread fixed costs.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Economies of scope occur when:
options: Producing two services together costs less than producing them separately
explanation: Passenger and freight sharing infrastructure is an example.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Average cost pricing in a natural monopoly is often used instead of marginal cost pricing because:
options: Marginal cost pricing would not cover total costs when average cost is declining
explanation: A subsidy would otherwise be required.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: A cost function in transport relates:
options: Total cost to output levels and input prices
explanation: Econometric estimation is used with operator data.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Indivisibility of transport infrastructure means that:
options: Capacity must be added in large lumps rather than continuously
explanation: This creates periods of excess capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Peak load pricing is justified because:
options: Peak users impose the capacity cost and higher congestion cost
Off peak users cause capacity cost
explanation: It spreads demand and defers capacity expansion.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Ramsey pricing sets mark ups over marginal cost:
options: Inversely proportional to the elasticity of demand of each market
explanation: It recovers fixed costs with least welfare loss.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Capital cost of a highway project includes:
options: Land, earthwork, pavement, structures, and design and supervision
explanation: Contingencies are also added.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Routine maintenance of a road refers to:
options: Regular small scale works such as pothole patching and drain clearing
explanation: Periodic maintenance includes overlays and resurfacing.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Deferring road maintenance typically leads to:
options: Much higher rehabilitation cost and increased vehicle operating cost
explanation: Deterioration accelerates once the surface fails.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Life cycle cost analysis of a pavement compares alternatives on the basis of:
options: Discounted agency and user costs over the analysis period
explanation: Rigid pavements may win despite higher initial cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Agency costs in life cycle costing refer to:
options: Costs borne by the authority for construction and maintenance
explanation: User costs include delay during work zones.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Work zone user costs during maintenance are caused by:
options: Delays, detours and increased vehicle operating and accident costs
explanation: Night working can reduce them.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Depreciation of a transport asset represents:
options: The loss of value of the asset over its service life
explanation: Straight line and declining balance methods are common.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Contingency allowance in a cost estimate is provided for:
options: Uncertainty in quantities, prices and unforeseen conditions
explanation: It reduces as design detail improves.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem: Cost overruns in transport megaprojects are commonly attributed to:
options: Optimism bias, scope changes and strategic misrepresentation
explanation: Reference class forecasting is a proposed remedy.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Accident costs in economic evaluation are usually valued using:
options: Willingness to pay for risk reduction or the human capital approach
explanation: Value of statistical life is derived this way.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Load factor of a transport service is:
options: The ratio of used capacity to available capacity
explanation: Higher load factor lowers cost per passenger.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Sunk costs should be excluded from future investment decisions.
explanation: Only incremental future costs and benefits are relevant to a decision.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem: Economies of density refer to expanding the network to new routes.
explanation: They refer to more traffic on a network of fixed size; scope and scale differ.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Capital, maintenance and life cycle costing of transport facilities
stem:
Assertion (A): Life cycle cost analysis may favour an alternative with higher initial cost.
Reason (R): Lower maintenance and user costs discounted over the service life can outweigh the extra first cost.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: The discount rate strongly influences the outcome.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost functions, economies of scale and density
stem:
Assertion (A): Marginal cost pricing in a natural monopoly leads to a financial deficit.
Reason (R): When average cost is falling, marginal cost lies below average cost and revenue cannot cover total cost.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Two part tariffs or subsidies are used.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

topic: Cost concepts and classification in transport
stem: Which of the following are external costs of road transport?
explanation: Fuel is an internal cost borne by the user.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 2

stem: A transport demand curve normally slopes downward because:
options: Higher generalised cost reduces the quantity of travel demanded
explanation: Users switch mode, route, time or destination.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Price elasticity of demand is defined as:
options: The percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price
explanation: It is usually negative for a normal good.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Demand is said to be inelastic when the absolute value of elasticity is:
explanation: Revenue then rises when price is increased.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Public transport fare elasticity in the short run is typically about:
explanation: Long run elasticities are larger in magnitude.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Cross elasticity of demand between car travel and bus travel is:
explanation: A rise in fuel price increases bus patronage.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Income elasticity of demand for car travel is generally:
options: Positive, since car use rises with income
explanation: Bus travel can be an inferior good in some contexts.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Equilibrium in a transport market occurs where:
options: The demand and supply or cost flow curves intersect
explanation: It determines the flow and generalised cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Induced or generated traffic after a road improvement occurs because:
options: Lower generalised cost makes new trips worthwhile
explanation: Ignoring it overstates time savings.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: The classical four stage transport model consists of:
options: Trip generation, distribution, modal split and assignment
explanation: It is applied to zones of a study area.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Trip generation models relate the number of trips to:
options: Land use and socio economic characteristics of the zone
explanation: Regression and category analysis are used.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: The gravity model of trip distribution assumes trips are:
options: Proportional to zonal attractions and inversely related to a function of travel cost
explanation: A deterrence function calibrates the distance effect.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: The logit model in modal split gives the probability of choosing a mode as a function of:
options: The utility of that mode relative to all alternatives
explanation: Utility includes cost, time and other attributes.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Stated preference surveys estimate demand by:
options: Asking respondents to choose among hypothetical alternatives
explanation: Revealed preference uses observed choices instead.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Trip assignment allocates trips to:
options: Specific routes on the network between origin and destination
explanation: All or nothing and equilibrium assignments are used.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Wardrop's first principle of equilibrium assignment states that:
options: No traveller can reduce travel time by unilaterally changing route
explanation: The second principle gives system optimum.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Time series and trend extrapolation forecasting is weak because it:
options: Assumes past relationships continue and ignores policy changes
explanation: It is still useful for short term forecasts.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Activity based models improve on the four stage approach by:
options: Modelling the sequence of daily activities and derived travel of individuals
explanation: They better capture scheduling and trip chaining.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: A transport supply function relates:
options: The generalised cost or travel time to the volume carried
explanation: Congestion makes cost rise with volume.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: The BPR volume delay function expresses travel time as:
options: Free flow time multiplied by a function of the volume to capacity ratio
explanation: It is widely used in equilibrium assignment.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: Capacity of a transport facility in economic terms represents:
options: The maximum flow beyond which cost rises very steeply
explanation: Supply curves become nearly vertical at capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: Marginal cost pricing of a congested road implies charging users:
options: The additional delay cost they impose on all other users
explanation: This is the basis of congestion pricing.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: A two part tariff in transport consists of:
options: A fixed access charge plus a usage related charge
explanation: It recovers fixed costs while keeping usage price near marginal cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: Price discrimination in transport services means:
options: Charging different prices to different users for essentially the same service
explanation: Airline yield management is a leading example.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: Subsidy to public transport is often justified on grounds of:
options: Second best pricing, scale economies and social equity
explanation: Underpriced car travel is a key second best argument.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: The Mohring effect refers to:
options: Increased frequency with more demand reducing waiting time for all users
explanation: It is an economy of scale in public transport.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem: Deregulation of transport markets is expected to:
options: Increase competition and efficiency but may reduce service in thin markets
explanation: Public service obligations address rural coverage.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Latent demand for travel refers to:
options: Trips people would make if the generalised cost were lower
explanation: It materialises when capacity is added.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Public transport fare elasticity is generally larger in the long run than the short run.
explanation: Users have more time to change car ownership, location and habits.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: The gravity model assumes trip interchange is independent of travel cost.
explanation: It assumes interchange declines with a deterrence function of travel cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

topic: Supply functions and pricing in transport markets
stem:
Assertion (A): Congestion pricing charges drivers more than their own perceived cost.
Reason (R): Each additional vehicle imposes delay on all other users which the driver does not otherwise pay for.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: The charge internalises the external cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem:
Assertion (A): Induced traffic must be considered when appraising road capacity expansion.
Reason (R): Lower generalised cost generates new trips that partly erode the expected time savings.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Ignoring it overstates project benefits.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Which are the stages of the classical four stage transport model?
explanation: Pavement design is not part of demand modelling.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 3

stem: Vehicle operating cost normally includes:
options: Fuel, lubricants, tyres, maintenance, depreciation and crew cost
explanation: Interest on capital is also included.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Fuel consumption is generally the largest single component of VOC for:
options: Heavy commercial vehicles on long hauls
explanation: Its share varies with fuel prices and vehicle type.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Tyre wear cost in VOC increases strongly with:
explanation: Side forces on curves accelerate wear.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Depreciation as a component of VOC depends on:
options: Vehicle utilisation, age and operating conditions
explanation: Poor roads shorten vehicle service life.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Crew cost is a significant part of VOC for:
options: Buses and trucks with paid drivers
explanation: It is largely time related rather than distance related.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Interest on the capital invested in a vehicle is included in VOC because:
options: The capital tied up has an opportunity cost
explanation: It is usually annualised over the vehicle life.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Time related VOC components are best expressed:
options: Per hour of vehicle use rather than per kilometre
explanation: Crew wages and part of depreciation are time related.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Overhead cost in commercial vehicle operation includes:
explanation: It is apportioned to vehicle kilometres.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Vehicle operating cost per kilometre generally:
explanation: Roughness is measured by the International Roughness Index.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Fuel consumption versus speed for a typical vehicle shows:
options: A U shaped curve with a minimum at an intermediate speed
explanation: Very low and very high speeds are both inefficient.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Rising and falling gradients increase VOC because:
options: Extra fuel is needed on the rise and braking wear occurs on the fall
explanation: Vertical alignment improvement can reduce VOC.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Speed change cycles caused by congestion increase VOC because of:
explanation: Excess fuel and brake and tyre wear result.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Horizontal curvature increases VOC because:
options: Side friction and speed reduction increase tyre wear and fuel use
explanation: Curvature is expressed as degrees per kilometre.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Vehicle age affects VOC by:
options: Increasing maintenance and fuel consumption while reducing reliability
explanation: Fleet renewal reduces operating cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Overloading of trucks affects the road and the operator by:
options: Accelerating pavement damage and increasing vehicle wear
explanation: Pavement damage rises with the fourth power of axle load.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Congestion increases the value of time component of transport cost because:
options: Travel takes longer and becomes less reliable
explanation: Reliability is valued in addition to mean time.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: The HDM-4 model is used to:
options: Predict road deterioration, vehicle operating costs and economic returns
explanation: It is widely used for road investment appraisal.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Mechanistic VOC models estimate fuel consumption from:
options: Forces resisting motion such as rolling, air, gradient and inertia
explanation: They can be transferred between countries more easily.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Empirical VOC relationships are derived from:
options: Field surveys of operators and controlled vehicle experiments
explanation: Local calibration is essential for transferability.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Road user cost studies in India by CRRI provide:
options: VOC relationships calibrated to Indian vehicles and road conditions
explanation: They are used in highway project appraisal.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Road user cost consists of:
options: Vehicle operating cost, travel time cost and accident cost
explanation: Savings in these form the benefits of improvement.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: VOC savings from a road improvement are computed as:
options: The difference in total VOC between the with and without project cases
explanation: Traffic growth over the analysis period is included.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: For economic analysis, vehicle operating costs should exclude:
options: Taxes and duties, which are transfer payments
explanation: Financial analysis retains taxes.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Sensitivity of VOC based benefits to fuel price assumptions is important because:
options: Fuel is a large and volatile component of operating cost
explanation: Scenario analysis is recommended.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Roughness progression models are needed in VOC analysis because:
options: Pavement condition worsens over time and VOC rises accordingly
explanation: Maintenance strategy is optimised against this.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Improving pavement surface condition from poor to good typically:
options: Reduces VOC substantially, often by a large percentage
explanation: This is the main benefit of periodic maintenance.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Lubricant consumption in VOC models is usually related to:
options: Fuel consumption and engine operating conditions
explanation: It is a small but non negligible component.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem: Vehicle operating cost increases as pavement roughness increases.
explanation: Fuel, tyre, maintenance and depreciation costs all rise with roughness.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Taxes and duties on fuel should be included in economic VOC estimates.
explanation: They are transfer payments and are excluded from economic, though not financial, analysis.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Factors affecting VOC: road and traffic conditions
stem:
Assertion (A): Fuel consumption per kilometre is minimum at an intermediate speed.
Reason (R): At very low speeds engine inefficiency dominates and at high speeds aerodynamic resistance dominates.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: The curve is therefore U shaped.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem:
Assertion (A): VOC relationships must be calibrated to local conditions.
Reason (R): Vehicle fleets, fuel prices, driving behaviour and road conditions differ greatly between countries.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: HDM-4 provides calibration levels for this purpose.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

stem: Which of the following are components of vehicle operating cost?
explanation: Construction cost is an agency cost, not a vehicle operating cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 4

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: Traffic congestion occurs when:
options: Demand approaches or exceeds the capacity of the facility
explanation: Travel times rise sharply near capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: Recurrent congestion is caused by:
options: Regular peak period demand exceeding capacity
explanation: Non recurrent congestion arises from incidents and events.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: The travel time index measures:
options: The ratio of peak period travel time to free flow travel time
explanation: Values above one indicate congestion.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: The volume to capacity ratio is used as:
options: An indicator of the level of service and congestion on a facility
explanation: Level of service F implies breakdown flow.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: Buffer time index reflects:
options: The extra time travellers must allow for reliable on time arrival
explanation: Reliability is valued separately from mean delay.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: Delay in congestion analysis is normally measured as:
options: Actual travel time minus the travel time at free flow or an acceptable speed
explanation: It is aggregated over all users to value congestion cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: Hypercongestion refers to the region of the speed flow curve where:
options: Both speed and flow are reduced as density increases beyond capacity
explanation: It represents unstable queued conditions.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: Shockwaves in traffic flow arise from:
options: Discontinuities between traffic states of different density
explanation: Queue formation and dissipation are shockwave phenomena.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: The congestion externality arises because a driver:
options: Considers only their own travel cost and not the delay imposed on others
explanation: Marginal social cost exceeds average private cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: The optimum congestion charge equals:
options: The difference between marginal social cost and average private cost at the optimum flow
explanation: It is a Pigouvian tax on the externality.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: Under unpriced congestion the equilibrium flow is:
options: Higher than the socially optimum flow
explanation: Deadweight loss results from over consumption.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: Downs Thomson or the fundamental law of road congestion suggests that:
options: Added road capacity is eventually absorbed by induced demand
explanation: Pricing or transit improvement is needed alongside capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: A cordon pricing scheme charges vehicles:
options: For crossing a defined boundary into a congested area
explanation: Singapore and London use variants of this.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: Distance based or time of day dynamic tolling is superior in theory because it:
options: Charges more closely in proportion to the congestion actually caused
explanation: Electronic tolling makes it feasible.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: A common equity criticism of congestion pricing is that it:
options: Bears more heavily on low income travellers who must drive
explanation: Revenue recycling to public transport can address it.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: Second best pricing arises when:
options: Not all modes or routes can be priced at marginal cost
explanation: Public transport subsidies are a second best response.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Travel demand management measures aim to:
options: Reduce or redistribute travel demand rather than add capacity
explanation: Staggered hours and car pooling are examples.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Parking pricing and supply control reduce congestion by:
options: Discouraging car trips to congested destinations
explanation: Cruising for parking is itself a source of traffic.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: High occupancy vehicle lanes are provided to:
options: Encourage car pooling and bus use by giving them a travel time advantage
explanation: HOT lanes allow paying single occupants to use spare capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Ramp metering on freeways works by:
options: Regulating the rate of entry to keep mainline flow below breakdown
explanation: It preserves throughput and delays breakdown.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Intelligent transport systems reduce congestion mainly through:
options: Better information, incident management and adaptive control
explanation: Adaptive signal control responds to real time flows.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Incident management programmes reduce non recurrent congestion by:
options: Detecting, responding to and clearing incidents quickly
explanation: Every minute of blockage causes several minutes of queue.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Land use policies help reduce congestion by:
options: Locating activities to shorten trips and support transit and walking
explanation: Mixed use and density support non car modes.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Public acceptability of congestion charging usually improves when:
options: Revenues are visibly used to improve transport alternatives
explanation: Trials often shift opinion after implementation.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Bus rapid transit reduces congestion cost by:
options: Providing high capacity segregated transit that attracts car users
explanation: Dedicated lanes give reliable travel times.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: Revenue from a congestion charge represents:
options: A transfer rather than a net economic benefit in itself
explanation: The efficiency gain is the reduced deadweight loss.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Nature and measurement of traffic congestion
stem: Total congestion cost to society is estimated from:
options: Aggregate delay valued at the value of time plus extra vehicle operating cost
explanation: Emissions cost may also be included.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem: Under unpriced congestion the traffic flow exceeds the socially optimal flow.
explanation: Drivers ignore the marginal external delay they impose on others.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Adding road capacity permanently eliminates congestion.
explanation: Induced demand tends to fill the new capacity over time.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

topic: Congestion externality and economics of pricing
stem:
Assertion (A): The optimal congestion toll equals marginal social cost minus average private cost.
Reason (R): Charging this difference makes the driver face the full social cost of the trip.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: It is a Pigouvian correction of the externality.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem:
Assertion (A): Ramp metering can increase the total throughput of a freeway.
Reason (R): Preventing the mainline from breaking down keeps flow near capacity rather than in the queued state.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Discharge flow after breakdown is lower than capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

stem: Which are travel demand management measures?
options: Staggered work hours and car pooling
explanation: Adding a lane is a capacity expansion, not demand management.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 5

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: An externality in transport is:
options: A cost or benefit imposed on third parties not reflected in market prices
explanation: Internalisation is a key policy objective.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Major environmental externalities of road transport include:
options: Air pollution, noise, greenhouse gases and habitat severance
explanation: Their valuation is required for full economic appraisal.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: The value of a statistical life used in accident cost valuation is derived from:
options: Willingness to pay for small reductions in fatality risk
explanation: The human capital approach is an alternative.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Noise cost from a road is usually valued using:
options: Hedonic property price studies or stated preference surveys
explanation: Property values fall with higher noise exposure.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: A carbon price used in transport appraisal represents:
options: The social cost of an additional tonne of carbon dioxide emitted
explanation: Values are set by government guidance.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Community severance caused by a new highway refers to:
options: The barrier effect separating parts of a community
explanation: Pedestrian crossings and underpasses mitigate it.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Local air pollution damage costs depend strongly on:
options: Population exposed and the pollutant concentration
explanation: Urban emissions cause much higher damage than rural ones.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Internalising an externality through a Pigouvian tax means:
options: Setting the tax equal to the marginal external damage
explanation: It restores the efficient level of activity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Wider economic impacts of transport projects include:
options: Agglomeration benefits, labour market effects and imperfect competition effects
explanation: They are additional to conventional user benefits.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Agglomeration economies arise because:
options: Firms and workers located closer together are more productive
explanation: Better transport effectively increases economic density.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Employment effects of a transport project during construction are:
options: Usually temporary and may displace jobs elsewhere
explanation: Care is needed to avoid overstating them.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Regional development effects of a new transport link may:
options: Benefit either region and sometimes draw activity away from the weaker one
explanation: This is called the two way road effect.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Land value uplift near a new transport facility mainly reflects:
explanation: Counting it in addition to user benefits risks double counting.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Freight transport improvements generate indirect benefits through:
options: Lower logistics cost, larger markets and improved supply chains
explanation: Just in time operation depends on reliable transport.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Tourism benefits of a transport project should be counted carefully because:
options: Much of the activity may be displaced from other regions
explanation: Only net national gains count in national appraisal.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
stem: Reliability benefits are increasingly included in appraisal because:
options: Travellers and shippers value predictable journey times in addition to average time
explanation: Standard deviation of travel time is used as a measure.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: Contingent valuation is a method that:
options: Asks people their willingness to pay for a non market good
explanation: It can value environmental and safety improvements.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: The hedonic pricing method values environmental quality by:
options: Analysing how property prices vary with environmental attributes
explanation: It requires a well functioning property market.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: Shadow pricing in economic analysis is used when:
options: Market prices are distorted by taxes, subsidies or controls
explanation: Border prices are used for traded goods.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: A build operate transfer concession means the private party:
options: Finances, builds and operates the facility before transferring it to government
explanation: Toll revenue usually repays the investment.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: Viability gap funding is provided to:
options: Make an economically desirable but financially unviable project attractive to investors
explanation: It is a capital grant limited to a share of project cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: An annuity or hybrid annuity model differs from a BOT toll concession because:
options: The authority pays the concessionaire instalments rather than the concessionaire taking traffic risk
explanation: It reduces demand risk for the private party.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: Fuel taxes as a policy instrument are attractive because they:
options: Are easy to collect and relate loosely to distance and emissions
explanation: They cannot differentiate by time and place of travel.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: Value capture financing for transport uses:
options: Betterment levies, development charges and property based taxes
explanation: It converts accessibility gains into project revenue.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Transportation Economics [101620], Unit 6

unit_title: Indirect Costs and Benefits of Transport Projects
topic: Valuation methods, financing and policy instruments
stem: Risk allocation in a public private partnership should place each risk with:

unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators

explanation: Integrated models such as LUTI represent this feedback.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction
stem: Accessibility as a planning indicator measures:
options: The ease of reaching opportunities such as jobs and services
explanation: It combines land use and transport network data.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction
stem: Mixed land use development helps infrastructure planning by:
options: Reducing trip lengths and balancing demand across the day
explanation: It supports walking and transit.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction
stem: Urban sprawl imposes higher infrastructure cost because:

explanation: Compact growth reduces per capita cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction
stem: Geographic information systems support infrastructure planning by:

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction

explanation: Satellite imagery gives repeated coverage.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators

explanation: They maximise ridership and land value capture.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction
stem: Carrying capacity based planning of a region considers:
options: Limits imposed by natural resources, environment and existing infrastructure
explanation: Water availability is often the binding constraint.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction
stem: Urban sprawl generally increases the per capita cost of infrastructure networks.
explanation: Longer networks serve fewer users per kilometre.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Econometric indicators and models in infrastructure planning
stem: A high R squared value in a regression proves that the relationship is causal.
explanation: It only measures explained variation; causality requires theory and identification.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
topic: Land use indicators and land use transport interaction
stem:
Assertion (A): Transit oriented development promotes higher densities near stations.
Reason (R): Concentrating population and jobs within walking distance maximises ridership and the return on the transit investment.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: It also supports land value capture financing.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
stem:
Assertion (A): Infrastructure indicators should be disaggregated by income group and gender.
Reason (R): Aggregate averages can conceal large disparities in who actually receives the service.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Equity objectives need disaggregated data.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Use of Econometric, Social and Land Use Indicators
stem: Which are social indicators used in infrastructure planning?

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: SWOT analysis in strategic planning examines:
explanation: It links internal capacity with the external environment.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: PESTEL analysis considers:

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Key performance indicators in a strategic plan should be:

explanation: They enable monitoring of progress.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure

explanation: It integrates fares, services and infrastructure.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales
stem: Utility coordination during road works is desirable because:

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales
stem: The water energy food nexus concept highlights that:

explanation: Integrated planning avoids unintended consequences.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales
stem: Spatial planning integrates infrastructure with development by:

explanation: Regional plans reserve corridors for future networks.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales
stem: A corridor approach to infrastructure development means:

explanation: Industrial corridors in India follow this model.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Public funding of infrastructure is typically drawn from:
explanation: Fiscal space limits the amount available.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Municipal bonds are used to:
options: Raise long term debt from capital markets for urban infrastructure
explanation: Credit rating of the municipality is essential.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: A public private partnership is defined by:
options: A long term contract with risk sharing and private performance based delivery
explanation: Payment is linked to output or availability.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: An availability payment PPP means the private party is paid:
options: For keeping the asset available to specified standards regardless of usage
explanation: Demand risk stays with the authority.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Value for money assessment in PPP compares:
options: The PPP option with a public sector comparator
explanation: Risk transfer is quantified in the comparison.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Infrastructure investment trusts allow:

explanation: They help developers recycle capital.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Asset monetisation of operating public infrastructure involves:

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: User charges for infrastructure services are justified because they:

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Green bonds finance projects that:

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Blended finance in infrastructure uses:

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: Monitoring and evaluation of a strategic plan requires:

explanation: Feedback allows the plan to be updated.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
stem: In an availability payment PPP the private party bears the demand risk.

source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales
stem: Institutional fragmentation improves coordination of infrastructure delivery.
explanation: Fragmentation causes duplication, gaps and poor coordination.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621]
unit_title: Integration of Strategic Planning for Infrastructure
topic: Integration across sectors, agencies and spatial scales
stem:
Assertion (A): Common utility ducts are provided along urban roads.
Reason (R): Repeated excavation by different utility agencies damages the pavement and disrupts traffic.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Coordinated provision reduces life cycle cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Infrastructure Planning and Design [101621], Unit 4
