subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: The Windsor probe test assesses concrete strength by measuring:
options: The depth of penetration of a driven steel probe
explanation: It is a penetration resistance method.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: Infrared thermography of a concrete deck detects delamination because:
options: Debonded areas heat and cool at a different rate from sound concrete
explanation: Surveys are best done during rapid heating or cooling.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: The linear polarisation resistance technique gives:
options: An estimate of the instantaneous corrosion rate of the steel
explanation: It complements half cell potential mapping.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: A rebar locator or profometer works on the principle of:
options: Electromagnetic induction responding to embedded steel
explanation: Congested reinforcement can cause misreadings.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: A core with a length to diameter ratio less than two gives:
options: A higher apparent strength requiring a correction factor
explanation: End restraint from the platens increases the measured value.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Principles and scope of non destructive testing
stem: Selection of an NDT method for a given investigation should be based on:
options: The property to be assessed, accessibility, accuracy needed and cost
explanation: A test plan should be prepared before site work.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Principles and scope of non destructive testing
stem: Number and location of test points in an NDT survey should be:
options: Statistically adequate and representative of the element and its variability
explanation: Codes prescribe minimum numbers of readings per location.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Surface hardness, ultrasonic and penetration methods
stem: A couplant such as grease is applied to UPV transducers to:
options: Ensure good acoustic contact with the concrete surface
explanation: Air gaps would strongly attenuate the pulse.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: Chloride content in NDT reporting is normally expressed as:
options: A percentage by mass of cement or of concrete
explanation: Thresholds are commonly quoted per mass of cement.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Surface hardness, ultrasonic and penetration methods
stem: Indirect surface transmission gives the most reliable ultrasonic pulse velocity.
explanation: Direct transmission with transducers on opposite faces is the most reliable arrangement.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: Core testing is regarded as the most reliable estimate of in situ strength.
explanation: It measures the actual concrete, subject to standard correction factors.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Surface hardness, ultrasonic and penetration methods
stem:
Assertion (A): A carbonated surface layer should be ground away before rebound hammer testing.
Reason (R): Carbonation hardens the surface skin and the instrument would then overestimate the strength.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Surface preparation is part of the standard procedure.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem:
Assertion (A): Low electrical resistivity of concrete indicates a high risk of rapid corrosion.
Reason (R): Low resistivity means ions move easily, allowing large corrosion currents between anode and cathode.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Resistivity is used with half cell potential data.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622]
unit_title: Non Destructive Testing Systems Non Destructive Testing Systems Use Of
topic: Electrical, radiographic and semi destructive methods
stem: Which of the following are semi destructive test methods for concrete?
explanation: UPV testing causes no damage at all.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Repair & Rehabilitation of Structures [101622], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The wing span of an aircraft primarily governs the design of:
options: Taxiway and runway separations and gate spacing
explanation: Wing tip clearance controls lateral separations.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The wheel base and wheel tread of an aircraft mainly affect:
options: Design of taxiway curves, fillets and turning radii
explanation: They determine the path of the main gear on turns.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The undercarriage or landing gear configuration mainly influences:
options: Pavement thickness design through load distribution
explanation: More wheels spread the load over a larger area.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: A dual tandem landing gear arrangement has:
options: Two wheels in line front to back on each of two struts
explanation: It reduces the load per wheel on the pavement.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The maximum take off weight of an aircraft governs:
options: Runway length requirement and pavement design
explanation: Heavier aircraft need longer runways and thicker pavements.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Tyre pressure of an aircraft mainly influences:
options: The stresses in the upper layers of the pavement
explanation: It affects the surface course and contact area.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The fuselage length of an aircraft affects the design of:
options: Apron gate positions and taxiway holding bay length
explanation: Nose in parking depth depends on it.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The tail height of an aircraft is critical for:
options: Clearance under hangars, jet bridges and obstacle limitation surfaces
explanation: Hangar door heights must accommodate the largest aircraft.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The runway length required increases with:
options: Higher airport elevation, higher temperature and upward gradient
explanation: All three reduce engine thrust or increase resistance.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Correction to basic runway length for elevation is normally taken as:
options: 7 percent increase per 300 m rise above mean sea level
explanation: Lower air density reduces lift and thrust.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Correction to runway length for temperature is applied at:
options: 1 percent for every 1 degree Celsius by which airport reference temperature exceeds standard
explanation: Standard temperature falls by 6.5 degrees per 1000 m.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The airport reference temperature is defined as:
options: Monthly mean of average daily temperature plus one third of difference from mean maximum for hottest month
explanation: It represents a hot day design condition.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: After elevation and temperature corrections, the total correction should not exceed:
options: 35 percent of the basic runway length before gradient correction
explanation: Beyond this a special aeronautical study is needed.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Correction for effective gradient of the runway is taken as:
options: 20 percent increase for every 1 percent effective gradient
explanation: Effective gradient is the difference in extreme elevations divided by length.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Balanced field length occurs when:
options: The accelerate stop distance equals the take off distance available
explanation: It corresponds to the critical engine failure speed.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The clearway is defined as:
options: A defined rectangular area beyond the runway, under airport control, free of obstacles
explanation: It permits part of the initial climb beyond the runway end.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: The stopway is:
options: A prepared area beyond the runway able to support an aborted take off
explanation: It need not support normal operations, only occasional stops.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: The ICAO aerodrome reference code consists of:
options: A code number based on reference field length and a code letter based on wing span and gear span
explanation: For example code 4E covers large wide body aircraft.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: Aerodrome reference code number 4 corresponds to an aeroplane reference field length of:
explanation: Code numbers 1 to 4 cover increasing field lengths.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: The design or critical aircraft for an airport is:
options: The most demanding aircraft expected to use the airport regularly
explanation: Substantial use is typically defined as 500 annual departures.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: The aeroplane reference field length is measured:
options: At sea level, standard atmosphere, still air and zero runway slope at maximum take off mass
explanation: It is a standardised comparison basis given by the manufacturer.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: The Pavement Classification Number and Aircraft Classification Number system is used to:
options: Report pavement strength and check aircraft compatibility
explanation: Operation is permitted if ACN does not exceed PCN.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: Wake turbulence categories of aircraft are based on:
explanation: They determine minimum separation between successive aircraft.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: An increase in the number of wheels in the landing gear generally:
options: Reduces the required pavement thickness for the same total load
explanation: The load is distributed over a wider area.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: Jet blast from aircraft engines requires:
options: Blast pads or protective surfaces at runway ends and behind parked aircraft
explanation: High velocity exhaust can erode unpaved surfaces.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: Aircraft mix at an airport influences:
options: Runway capacity because of separation requirements between different categories
explanation: A heterogeneous mix reduces the hourly capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Landing runway length requirement depends on:
options: Approach speed, landing weight and braking or stopping ability
explanation: A safety factor is applied to the demonstrated distance.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Runway length must be increased by 7 percent for every 300 m rise in elevation.
explanation: Reduced air density at altitude lowers lift and engine thrust.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem: The aerodrome reference code letter is based on aircraft weight.
explanation: The code letter is based on wing span and outer main gear wheel span.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem:
Assertion (A): Wing span is a controlling parameter for taxiway separation distances.
Reason (R): Adequate wing tip clearance must be maintained between an aircraft on a taxiway and adjacent objects.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Separation standards are tabulated against the code letter.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
topic: Aircraft classification and design aircraft selection
stem:
Assertion (A): The critical or design aircraft governs the geometric and pavement design of an airport.
Reason (R): The facility must safely accommodate the most demanding aircraft making substantial regular use of it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Occasional larger movements may be handled by special procedures.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Characteristics Related to Airport Design
stem: Which factors increase the required runway length?
explanation: A headwind reduces the required length.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 1

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Which of the following is a major consideration in airport site selection?
options: Availability of obstruction free approach zones
explanation: Approach and take off surfaces must be clear.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: An airport site should preferably have soil that is:
options: Well drained with adequate bearing capacity
explanation: Poor soils increase pavement and drainage cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Airports should be located away from bird attracting activities because:
options: Bird strikes are a serious hazard to aircraft
explanation: Garbage dumps and slaughterhouses must be avoided nearby.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Noise considerations in airport siting are addressed by:
options: Compatible land use zoning around the approach and departure paths
explanation: Noise contours guide permissible development.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Regional planning aspects of airport siting include:
options: Surface access to the city and interference with other airports
explanation: Airspace conflicts with nearby aerodromes must be avoided.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Provision for future expansion at an airport site requires:
options: Reserving adequate land around the initial development
explanation: Master planning identifies the ultimate layout.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: Runways are oriented so that aircraft:
options: Take off and land into the direction of the prevailing wind
explanation: Headwind shortens the required runway length.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: A wind rose diagram represents:
options: Direction, duration and intensity of wind at a site
explanation: Data of at least five years should be used.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: The usability factor of a runway as recommended by ICAO should be at least:
explanation: An additional crosswind runway is provided if it is not met.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: The permissible crosswind component for aircraft with a reference field length of 1500 m or more is:
explanation: Smaller aircraft have lower permissible components.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: Type II wind rose analysis is used to determine:
options: The best runway orientation giving maximum usability against crosswind limits
explanation: A transparent strip template is rotated over the diagram.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: An open V runway configuration consists of:
options: Two runways in different directions that diverge from a near common point
explanation: It provides high capacity when winds are light.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: Parallel runway configurations increase capacity most when they are:
options: Widely spaced enough for independent simultaneous operations
explanation: Spacing requirements depend on instrument approach procedures.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: Intersecting runways reduce capacity because:
options: Operations on one runway must be coordinated with the other at the crossing
explanation: They are used where strong winds occur in multiple directions.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: Runway designation numbers are based on:
options: Magnetic azimuth of the runway centre line rounded to the nearest ten degrees, divided by ten
explanation: Reciprocal ends differ by 18.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: Parallel runways are distinguished in their designation by:
options: Letters L, C and R appended to the number
explanation: They denote left, centre and right.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: The primary function of a taxiway is to:
options: Provide access between runways, aprons and other facilities
explanation: Taxiways should minimise runway occupancy time.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: An exit taxiway placed at an acute angle of about 30 degrees to the runway is called:
explanation: It permits higher turn off speeds and raises capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: A parallel taxiway alongside a runway is provided to:
options: Avoid aircraft back tracking on the runway and increase capacity
explanation: It is essential at busy airports.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: Turning radius of a taxiway curve is governed by:
options: The speed of the aircraft and its wheel base
explanation: Fillets widen the pavement at the curve.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: The maximum longitudinal gradient of a taxiway is generally kept lower than that of a runway because:
options: Aircraft manoeuvre at low speed and gradient changes must be gentle
explanation: Sight distance and drainage also govern.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: Airport capacity is usually expressed as:
options: The number of passengers per year only
The number of aircraft operations that can be handled per hour
explanation: Practical capacity accepts a tolerable level of delay.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: Runway capacity is most strongly reduced by:
options: Instrument meteorological conditions and a heterogeneous aircraft mix
explanation: Separation minima increase under IFR conditions.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: A holding bay near the runway threshold allows:
options: Aircraft to wait or be overtaken without blocking the taxiway
explanation: It improves operational flexibility during peak periods.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: An airport master plan is:
options: A long term development concept for the ultimate airport layout
explanation: It is periodically reviewed as forecasts change.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: Zoning laws around an airport are enacted primarily to:
options: Restrict the height of structures and control incompatible land use
explanation: They protect obstacle limitation surfaces.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Topographic surveys for airport siting are needed to assess:
options: Earthwork quantities, drainage and obstruction heights
explanation: Level terrain reduces grading cost.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem: ICAO recommends a minimum runway usability factor of 95 percent.
explanation: If the main runway cannot achieve it, a crosswind runway is added.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: A rapid exit taxiway reduces runway occupancy time.
explanation: The acute angle allows aircraft to leave the runway at higher speed.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway orientation, wind rose and configurations
stem:
Assertion (A): A crosswind runway is provided at some airports.
Reason (R): When the primary runway alone cannot give the required usability factor, an additional orientation is needed.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: The wind rose analysis determines the need.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem:
Assertion (A): Waste disposal sites are not permitted close to airports.
Reason (R): They attract large numbers of birds and greatly increase the risk of bird strikes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Wildlife hazard management is part of airport safety.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway layout, capacity and airport classification
stem: Which measures increase the capacity of a runway system?
options: Providing a parallel full length taxiway
Adding a widely spaced parallel runway
explanation: A more diverse mix increases separation needs and lowers capacity.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 2

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: The width of a runway for aerodrome code letter E is usually:
explanation: Width increases with the code number and letter.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: The maximum longitudinal gradient of a runway for code number 4 as per ICAO is:
explanation: Steeper gradients increase the required length substantially.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: Effective gradient of a runway is defined as:
options: Difference between highest and lowest centre line elevations divided by the runway length
explanation: It is used for the runway length correction.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: The transverse or camber gradient of a runway is provided to:
options: Drain surface water quickly from the pavement
explanation: It is typically limited to about 1.5 percent.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: Rate of change of longitudinal gradient on a runway is limited to ensure:
options: Adequate sight distance and comfortable transition for aircraft
explanation: Vertical curves must satisfy a minimum length per percent change.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: Sight distance requirement on a runway for code number 3 or 4 requires that:
options: Any two points 3 m above the runway are mutually visible over half the runway length
explanation: It ensures aircraft on the runway can see each other.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: A displaced threshold on a runway is provided when:
options: Obstacles in the approach prevent use of the full runway for landing
explanation: The full length remains available for take off.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: Runway shoulders are provided to:
options: Resist erosion from jet blast and support aircraft that run off the pavement
explanation: They are usually paved for large aircraft.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: The runway strip is:
options: A defined area including the runway and stopway intended to reduce risk to aircraft running off
explanation: It must be graded and free of obstacles.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: Runway End Safety Area is provided:
options: Beyond the end of the runway strip to reduce damage in an overrun or undershoot
explanation: A minimum length of 90 m is normally required.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: The approach surface of the obstacle limitation surfaces is:
options: A horizontal plane over the runway
An inclined plane sloping upward from the end of the inner edge before the threshold
explanation: Its slope depends on the approach type and code number.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: The transitional surface in obstacle limitation extends:
options: Upward and outward from the sides of the strip and approach surface to the inner horizontal surface
explanation: It protects aircraft deviating laterally.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: The conical surface in obstacle limitation:
options: Slopes upward and outward from the periphery of the inner horizontal surface
explanation: Together the surfaces define the protected airspace.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: The take off climb surface protects:
options: The airspace required by a departing aircraft during its initial climb
explanation: Its divergence and slope are code dependent.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: An object that penetrates an obstacle limitation surface must be:
options: Removed, lowered, or if unavoidable marked and lighted
explanation: An aeronautical study may permit some penetrations.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: The clearway width as per ICAO extends laterally at least:
options: 75 m on each side of the extended runway centre line
explanation: Its slope must not exceed 1.25 percent upward.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: Graded portion of the runway strip must be able to:
options: Support an aircraft running off the runway without causing structural damage
explanation: Bearing strength and grading are specified in Annex 14.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: Taxiway width for code letter E is normally:
explanation: Width is governed by the outer main gear wheel span.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: The main gear wheel to taxiway edge clearance for large aircraft must be:
options: Sufficient to keep the wheels on the pavement when the cockpit follows the centre line
explanation: It governs the minimum taxiway width standard.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: Taxiway fillets are provided at junctions and curves to:
options: Provide extra pavement so the main gear stays on the surface during turns
explanation: Judgemental oversteering by pilots is assumed.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: The runway to parallel taxiway separation distance depends on:
options: The aerodrome code and wing span so that the taxiing aircraft clears the runway strip
explanation: Instrument runways need greater separation.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: Maximum longitudinal gradient of a taxiway for code number 3 or 4 is:
explanation: Taxiway grades are kept gentler than runway grades.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: A taxiway strip is provided to:
options: Protect an aircraft operating on the taxiway and reduce damage on a runoff
explanation: Its graded portion must be free of obstacles.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: A taxilane differs from a taxiway in that it:
options: Provides access within an apron area only
explanation: Lower separation standards apply to taxilanes.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: The runway holding position marking indicates:
options: Where an aircraft must stop before entering the runway unless cleared
explanation: Its distance from the centre line depends on the code number.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem: A rapid exit taxiway requires a minimum turn off radius so that:
options: Aircraft can leave the runway safely at the design exit speed
explanation: Typical exit speeds are around 90 km/h.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: A blast pad at the runway end is provided to:
options: Resist erosion from jet blast during take off run up
explanation: It is not designed for regular aircraft loading.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: The runway end safety area is intended to reduce damage during overruns and undershoots.
explanation: It provides a cleared and graded area beyond the strip end.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Runway geometric standards: length, width, gradients
stem: The transverse gradient of a runway is provided mainly to increase length.
explanation: It is provided for rapid drainage of surface water.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Taxiway geometric design and separation standards
stem:
Assertion (A): Fillets are provided at taxiway curves and intersections.
Reason (R): Extra pavement is needed to keep the main landing gear on the surface as the cockpit follows the centre line.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Fillet size increases with aircraft wheel base.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem:
Assertion (A): Obstacle limitation surfaces are defined around an aerodrome.
Reason (R): They establish the airspace that must remain free of obstacles for safe approach, circling and departure.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Height zoning laws enforce them on the ground.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Safety areas, strips, RESA and obstacle limitation surfaces
stem: Which of the following are obstacle limitation surfaces?
explanation: A shoulder is a pavement feature, not an airspace surface.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 3

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: A holding apron is normally located:
options: Adjacent to the runway end near the taxiway entrance
explanation: It allows final checks before entering the runway.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: The principal function of a holding apron is to permit:
options: Final engine run up and instrument checks and bypassing of aircraft
explanation: It prevents delays to following departures.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: A holding bay increases runway capacity because it:
options: Allows an aircraft not ready for departure to be overtaken
explanation: Departure sequencing becomes flexible.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Size of a holding apron is determined by:
options: The number and size of aircraft to be held and required clearances
explanation: Space for one aircraft to bypass another is needed.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Aircraft on a holding apron must be positioned so that:
options: Jet blast does not affect other aircraft or the runway strip
explanation: Blast orientation is a layout criterion.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: The runway holding position on a taxiway is located at a distance from the runway centre line that:
options: Depends on the code number and whether the runway is instrument or non instrument
explanation: Instrument runways require greater distances to protect the ILS.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: An ILS critical area near the runway must be kept clear because:
options: Aircraft or vehicles there can distort the localiser and glide path signals
explanation: Holding positions are set outside this area.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Pavement of a holding apron must be designed for:
options: Stationary aircraft loads with engines running, often more severe than moving loads
explanation: Prolonged static loading and blast govern the design.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: The apron is the area of an airport used for:
options: Loading, unloading, fuelling, parking and maintenance of aircraft
explanation: It links the terminal to the taxiway system.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: A frontal or linear apron concept places:
options: Aircraft gates along the face of a linear terminal building
explanation: It is simple and easily expanded lengthwise.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: A pier or finger apron layout:
options: Extends concourses into the apron with aircraft parked on both sides
explanation: It gives many gates but long walking distances.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: A satellite apron layout has:
options: A separate building surrounded by aircraft, connected to the terminal by a corridor
explanation: Underground or elevated connectors are used.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: A remote or open apron requires:
options: Bus or apron transfer of passengers to the terminal
explanation: It is economical and flexible for aircraft parking.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Apron size depends primarily on:
options: Number of gate positions, aircraft size, clearances and taxilane requirements
explanation: Peak hour aircraft demand determines gate numbers.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Gate occupancy time directly influences:
options: The number of gate positions required for a given demand
explanation: Longer turnarounds require more gates.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Nose in parking of aircraft at a gate requires:
options: A tractor for pushback but needs less apron depth and reduces blast on the terminal
explanation: Power out configurations avoid tugs but need more space.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Angled nose out parking is characterised by:
options: Self manoeuvring departure but greater blast and apron area requirement
explanation: It suits smaller aircraft and remote stands.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: A passenger boarding bridge or aerobridge connects:
options: The terminal building directly to the aircraft door
explanation: It improves passenger comfort and reduces apron traffic.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: Apron markings include:
options: Lead in lines, stop bars, stand numbers and equipment restraint lines
explanation: They guide safe manoeuvring and ground handling.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: A visual docking guidance system on an apron helps the pilot to:
options: Stop the aircraft accurately at the correct position on the stand
explanation: Accurate stopping is required for the boarding bridge.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: Hydrant fuelling systems on an apron:
options: Deliver fuel through underground pipelines to stands reducing tanker traffic
explanation: They improve safety and turnaround speed at busy airports.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: Apron drainage must handle:
options: Storm water and possible spillage of fuel and de icing fluid
explanation: Interceptors are needed to prevent pollution.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: Rigid pavement is often preferred on aprons because:
options: Static loads and fuel spillage damage flexible pavements
explanation: Concrete resists creep and fuel attack.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: Apron gradients are kept small but sufficient to:
options: Provide drainage while permitting safe servicing of aircraft
explanation: Excessive slope is unsafe for ground equipment.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: An isolated aircraft parking position is provided for:
options: Aircraft suspected of unlawful interference or carrying hazards
explanation: It is located well away from other facilities.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: A de icing pad located near the runway end is preferred because:
options: Holdover time after treatment is used efficiently before take off
explanation: Fluid must be collected and treated.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Clearance between a parked aircraft and a fixed object on an apron is specified to:
options: Prevent collision during manoeuvring and servicing
explanation: Clearances increase with the code letter.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: A holding apron allows an aircraft not ready for departure to be bypassed.
explanation: This flexibility improves runway utilisation and departure sequencing.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
topic: Apron operations, servicing and pavement considerations
stem: Flexible pavement is generally preferred on aprons over rigid pavement.
explanation: Static aircraft loads and fuel spillage favour rigid concrete pavement.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem:
Assertion (A): The runway holding position is set farther back on instrument runways.
Reason (R): Aircraft or vehicles close to the runway can interfere with the localiser and glide path signals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: ILS critical and sensitive areas must be protected.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem:
Assertion (A): Nose in parking reduces the apron depth required at a terminal.
Reason (R): The aircraft is pushed back by a tug instead of manoeuvring out under its own power.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Jet blast on the terminal is also reduced.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
stem: Which are recognised apron and terminal concepts?
explanation: The wind rose relates to runway orientation.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 4

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: In nose in parking the aircraft is:
options: Parked perpendicular to the terminal with its nose towards the building
explanation: Departure requires a pushback tractor.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: Angled nose in parking is used because it:
options: Allows easier manoeuvring while keeping the aircraft near the terminal
explanation: It needs more apron area than pure nose in.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: Parallel parking of aircraft at a terminal is:
options: Easiest for manoeuvring but requires the largest apron frontage per aircraft
explanation: Both doors of the aircraft can be used.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: The number of gates required at a terminal is estimated from:
options: Peak hour aircraft arrivals and average gate occupancy time with a utilisation factor
explanation: Gate use efficiency is typically 60 to 80 percent.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: Gate occupancy time for a wide body aircraft is generally:
options: Longer than for a narrow body aircraft
explanation: More passengers, baggage and fuel are handled.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: Power out parking configurations are less favoured at busy terminals because:
options: Jet blast and noise affect the terminal and adjacent stands
explanation: Nose in with pushback is the common practice.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: A MARS or multiple aircraft ramp system stand allows:
options: One wide body or two narrow body aircraft to use the same stand area
explanation: It gives flexibility as the fleet mix varies.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Aircraft parking configurations and gate requirements
stem: Gate assignment planning aims to:
options: Minimise passenger walking distance and aircraft delay while respecting stand compatibility
explanation: Common use gates improve utilisation.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Passenger terminal system: components and flows
stem: The access interface of a passenger terminal system includes:
options: Kerbside, parking and public transport facilities
explanation: It is where passengers transfer from ground transport.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System
topic: Passenger terminal system: components and flows
stem: The processing component of a terminal includes:
options: Check in, security screening, immigration, customs and baggage claim
explanation: Processing capacity governs terminal level of service.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623], Unit 5

subject_name: Program Elective: Airport Planning and Design [101623]
unit_title: Aircraft Parking Configurations Aircraft Parking Configurations The Passenger Terminal System

options: Based at a separate infrastructure depot with access to the running line at night
explanation: Track machines work in the nightly possession window.

stem: Noise mitigation at a depot located near housing includes:

unit_title: Basic Design and Construction of Rolling Stock Maintenance Facilities
topic: Depot planning: location, sizing and functions
stem: HSR depots can be laid out with short stabling roads of about 100 m.
explanation: Trainsets up to 400 m long require correspondingly long roads.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: High Speed Rail Engineering [101624], Unit 6

subject_name: Program Elective: High Speed Rail Engineering [101624]
unit_title: Basic Design and Construction of Rolling Stock Maintenance Facilities
stem:
Assertion (A): A strict permit to work and earthing procedure applies before roof level work in depots.
Reason (R): The 25 kV overhead line must be isolated and earthed or staff working on the roof risk electrocution.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Some depot roads are left unelectrified for this reason.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: High Speed Rail Engineering [101624], Unit 6

subject_name: Program Elective: High Speed Rail Engineering [101624]
unit_title: Basic Design and Construction of Rolling Stock Maintenance Facilities
topic: Depot planning: location, sizing and functions
stem:
Assertion (A): Rolling stock depots are located close to a terminal of the high speed line.
Reason (R): Empty running to and from the depot consumes capacity and operating cost without earning revenue.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
explanation: Access must be grade separated where possible.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: High Speed Rail Engineering [101624], Unit 6

subject_name: Program Elective: High Speed Rail Engineering [101624]
unit_title: Basic Design and Construction of Rolling Stock Maintenance Facilities
stem: Which facilities are typically provided in a high speed rolling stock depot?
options: Inspection pits and roof access gantries
explanation: A RESA is an airport feature.
source: BEU syllabus — Program Elective: High Speed Rail Engineering [101624], Unit 6
